hook.line: Tomás and Vale are looking at the sales numbers, and "more" is no longer enough. They want to say that things keep growing, and that the more they earn, the more they spend. Spanish has neat ways to say both.
hook.en: There are more and more tourists.

examples.en: There are more and more tourists.
The more I work, the less I sleep.
The more he earns, the more he spends.
The earlier you arrive, the better. (to a friend)

rule:
Two tools for talking about change.

*Cada vez más / menos*: more and more, less and less. English repeats the word; Spanish adds *cada vez*. It also sits in front of an adjective: *Cada vez es más caro.*

*Mientras más..., más...*: the more..., the more... *Mientras más trabajo, menos duermo.* Both halves start with *más* or *menos*, with a comma in the middle. It can end with just *mejor* or *peor*: *Mientras más temprano llegas, mejor.*

Spanish never adds "the" in these. In books and formal speech you will also see *cuanto más...* for the same idea.
smallPrint: Teachers call *mientras más..., más...* a proportional comparison, and *cada vez más* a progressive one.

options: There are fewer and fewer tourists.
There are more and more tourists.
The more I work, the more I sleep.
The more I work, the less I sleep.
The more he earns, the more he spends.
The more he earns, the less he spends.
The more you read, the worse you speak.
The more you read, the better you speak.
I'm more and more tired. (a man speaking)
I'm less and less tired. (a man speaking)

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right form and type the whole sentence (There are more and more tourists): ___ hay más turistas. (Cada vez / Mientras)
Type in Spanish: It rains less and less.
Type in Spanish: The more I work, the less I sleep.
yourTurn.why: *Mientras más* opens the first half and *menos* opens the second.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The more he earns, the more he spends.
yourTurn.why: Both halves start with *más*, with a comma between.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The earlier you arrive, the better. (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: The second half can be just *mejor*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Hernando comes less and less.
yourTurn.why: *Cada vez menos* after the verb says "less and less".

yourTurn.prompt: Make it "more and more": Cada vez es menos caro.
yourTurn.why: Swap *menos* for *más* and the meaning flips.

pitfalls.why: Almost. English repeats "more and more", but Spanish uses *cada vez más*.

pitfalls.wrong: Mientras más trabajo, el menos duermo.
pitfalls.why: Spanish doesn't add "the"; the second half just starts with *menos*.
In this pattern *más* comes right after *mientras*, before the verb.

personal: Say something that is changing in your life with *cada vez más* or *cada vez menos*, or a *mientras más..., más...* sentence.
